title: Agentic Postgres database access policy
description: Which local unix account may obtain which access profile of which project, read by the release-side broker (ADR 0043). Root-owned at /etc/agentic-postgres/database-access-policy.json, mode 0600, published atomically. It contains identifiers only -- account names, project keys and profile names -- and never a secret value, a role password or a connection string. A host with no policy file has no delegated access at all; that is the closed state, and it is why an absent file is an error rather than an empty allowance.

grants.description: May be empty. An empty list is a host that delegates nothing, which is a different statement from a missing file and has to be expressible.

grant.description: One account, one project, an enumerated set of profiles. There is deliberately no wildcard in any of the three fields. A grant that matched every project would silently cover projects deployed months later by someone else, which is the opposite of a decision an operator made; and a grant that matched every profile would hand out migration authority as a side effect of asking for runtime access.

unix_user.description: A local account name, matching the pattern host.schema.json uses for ssh.operator_user. Resolved from SUDO_UID by the broker rather than taken from an argument: a caller-supplied identity is not an identity.

project_key.description: The same shape outputs.schema.json calls projectKey. Enumerated, never a pattern: see the note on wildcards above.

profiles.description: Which profiles this account may obtain for this project. `migration_direct` is the one that carries schema authority, so it is written down separately rather than implied by holding any direct access at all.

accessProfileName.description: The three profiles ADR 0041 defines. An enum rather than a pattern, because the profile name selects which secret the broker reads: a free-form string here would be an arbitrary secret name arriving from a file.
